ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=80^\circ$, $\angle ACB=50^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle A$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $\angle ABC=80^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=50^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle A=180^\circ - \angle ABC - \angle ACB=\boxed{50^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: A, B, and C form the outer triangle, while point P and segments BP and PC are internal auxiliary markings with no given angle data. Use the text values ∠B = 80° and ∠C = 50°. Imagine extending one side through A to form an exterior angle at A. By the exterior angle theorem, that exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 80° + 50° = 130°.
